Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:10:1.english: I cast - I sowed six se'ah in it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:10:2.hebrew: חוזר - דמקח טעות הוא, דהא בהדיא פי' בחזקת כן, ואינו כן. וכיון שהמקח טעות הוא, אפי' בטיל להו אגב ארעא, חוזר; דנהי דאימעיט קרקעות מדין אונאה, מדין מקח טעות לא אימעיט, שהרי אין זה מכר, דאדעתא דהכי לא זבן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:10:2.english: It is reversed - For it is a mistaken transaction, since he explicitly specified [it] on the presumption that this was so, and it is not so. And since the transaction is mistaken, even [when the seeds] are nullified as subordinate to the land, it is reversed; for although land was excluded from the law of exploitation, it was not excluded from the law of a mistaken transaction, since this is not a [valid] sale, as he did not buy [it] with this intention.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:11:1.hebrew: כדבעי לה - כמה שצריך לקרקע, דמידי דאומדנא דשכיח דטעו הוי כדין אונאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:11:1.english: As required for it - As much as is needed for the land; for a matter of estimation, where it is common to err, is subject to the law of exploitation [ona'ah].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:12:1.hebrew: נשבעין עליהן - אם הודה במקצת, כגון טענו, פסקת עמי לזרוע ו' שמסרתי לך וזרעת חמש, והוא אומר, זרעתי חמש ומחצה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:12:1.english: Does one take an oath with regard to them - If he admitted to part [of the claim], for example, [the owner] claimed against him: "You agreed with me to sow six [measures] that I handed over to you, and you sowed [only] five," and he says: "I sowed five and a half."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:13:1.hebrew: עומר מתירן - קס"ד אגידולין דידהו קמיבעיא ליה, ולהכי קמהדר, אי דאשרוש קודם לעומר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:13:1.english: Does the omer permit them - We initially assumed [that Rava] is asking regarding their growth, and therefore [the Gemara] responds: "If they took root before the omer..."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:13:2.hebrew: תנינא - דעומר מתיר את גידוליהן במסכת מנחות (דף עא.), והתם מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:13:2.english: We learned - that the omer permits their growth in tractate Menachot (71a), and there [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:13:3.english: And if they did not take root - At the time of bringing the omer [offering].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:13:4.english: We learned - that the omer does not permit them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:14:1.hebrew: דחצדינהו - מן החדש, והיו צריכין שיתירם עומר לאכילה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:14:1.english: Where one reaped them - [From] the new [grain], and they required that the omer [offering] permit them for eating.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:14:2.english: And he sowed them prior to the omer - And the omer passed over them when they had not taken root.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:1:1.hebrew: קדשים שחייב באחריותן - אמר "הרי עלי עולה", והפרישה, והוממה ומכרה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:1:1.english: Sacrificial animals for which one bears responsibility - [For example, where] he said, "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt offering," and he set it aside, and it became blemished, and he sold it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:1:2.hebrew: יש להן אונאה - דכיון דאם מתה או נגנבה חייב באחריותה, דידיה היא, ו"אל תונו איש את אחיו" קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:1:2.english: They are subject to overreaching - Since if [the animal] dies or is stolen he is liable for its replacement, it is [considered] his, and we apply to it [the verse], "Do not wrong one another."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:1:3.english: And [sacrifices] for which he does not bear responsibility - For example, where he says, "Behold, this [animal]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:1:4.english: Even one who sells a Torah scroll, etc. - [It] explains the reason in the Gemara, in a baraita.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:2:1.english: An item acquired from hand to hand - [Scripture] warned regarding it with "Do not exploit."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:2:2.hebrew: שהוקשו לקרקעות - [דכתיב] והתנחלתם אותם וגו' (ויקרא כה), הוקשו לאחוזה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:2:2.english: As they are juxtaposed to land - As it is written: “And you shall bequeath them,” etc. (Leviticus 25[:46]) — they are juxtaposed to an ancestral possession [of land].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:1.english: From here [the Sages] said - Since documents were not excluded except because their physical substance is not bought and sold.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:2.hebrew: המוכר שטרותיו לבשם - לצור בהם אבקת סממנין, נמצא ממכרן של אלו לצורך תשמיש גופן הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:2.english: One who sells his documents to a perfumer - To wrap spice powder in them; thus, the sale of these [documents] is for the use of their [physical] substance.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:3.english: They are subject to price fraud - Because their physical substance is bought and sold.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:4.english: Obvious - How is [this] different from all ordinary movable property?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:5.hebrew: לפרוטות - סתם מוכר שטרות לבשם, אין שם המקח של איסר ביחד, אלא של פרוטות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:3:5.english: For perutot - Ordinarily, [when] one sells documents to a perfumer, the purchase there is not [worth] an issar altogether, but rather [only] perutot.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:4:1.hebrew: ידו ממש הוא - דקדייקת לעיל ״מיד עמיתך״, מטלטלים דוקא, הנקחין מיד אל יד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:4:1.english: [Does it mean] his actual hand - [How can you say that,] since you inferred above [from] "from your colleague’s hand" [that it refers] specifically [to] movable property, which is acquired from hand to hand?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:4:2.hebrew: הכא נמי מרשות - עמיתך קאמר, ואפילו קרקעות נמי במשמע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:4:2.english: Here too, from the possession - [of] your colleague [is what] it means, and even land is also included.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:5:1.english: I do not have - [a case where] he is obligated [to pay] double.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:5:2.english: Except - [That is, only] when he took it in his hand.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:5:3.hebrew: גגו חצירו [קרפיפו] מנין - שאם נכנסה שם ונעל בפניה לגנבה, מנין שקנתה לו חצירו ומתחייב כפל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:5:3.english: His roof, his courtyard, [his enclosure,] from where - [Meaning] that if [an animal] entered there and he locked [the entrance] before it to steal it, from where [do we know] that his courtyard acquired [it] for him and he becomes liable [for] double [payment]?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:5:4.hebrew: ת"ל ונתן מ"מ - מדלא כתיב ובידה יתננו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:5:4.english: The verse states: "And he shall place [it]," in any case - Since it is not written, "and into her hand shall he place it."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:7:1.english: And it is different there - [Referring to the verse:] “And he took all his land.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:9:1.english: They are subject to overcharging - If he sold them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:9:2.hebrew: בטלינהו אגב ארעא - ואין אונאה לקרקעות, ובשלא השרישו קאי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 56b:9:2.english: He subordinated them to the ground - and there is no [law of] overcharging for land; and [the dilemma] refers to [a case] where they have not taken root.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:10:1.hebrew: כל דבר שבמדה כו' אפילו פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר - הכא משמע דרבא מיירי אף בקרקעות, וכן נמי פרק האיש מקדש (קדושין דף מב: ושם ד"ה ה"ג) דקאמר: "ובמקרקעי נמי לא אמרינן אלא דפליג באומדנא, אבל פליג במשחתא אפילו פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר, דאמר רבא כל דבר שבמדה חוזר". ו"חוזר" דקאמר, היינו שהמקח בטל לגמרי, כדמוכח ריש התודה (מנחות דף עז.) ושלהי הספינה (ב"ב דף צ.). וקשה: דבפרק בית כור (בבא בתרא דף קד. ושם ד"ה פחות) תנן: "בית כור עפר אני מוכר לך מדה בחבל, פיחת כל שהוא ינכה, הותיר כל שהוא יחזור", ופירש רשב"ם התם דהא דאמר רבא דחוזר, מילתיה לא הוי בקרקעות — וקשה לפירושו מהכא! וי"ל: דהתם אינו אומר המוכר "מדדתי שיש בה בית כור", דאז ודאי היה חוזר כדרבא, אלא סתמא אומר כך, וסבור היה המוכר שיש כך, ולכך המקח קיים. וא"ת: לימא דידע דשדא שיתא ומוכרו יותר משויו, וכיון דזרעינהו דלמא בטל אגב קרקע? וי"ל: בענין זה פשיטא דיש אונאה, שהמכר אינו תלוי בקרקע אלא בחטי שבשוק:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:10:1.english: Any item that is [sold] by measure, etc., even less than the measure of exploitation, [the transaction] is reversed - Here it is implied that Rava is speaking even regarding land, and so too in the chapter [entitled] HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 42b, and there, s.v. "Hachi garsinan"), where [the Gemara] says: "And regarding land as well, we only say [there is no exploitation] when one divided by estimation; however, when one divided by measurement, even less than the measure of exploitation is reversed, as Rava said: Any item that is [sold] by measure is reversed." And "is reversed" that [Rava] says means that the sale is completely nullified, as is proven in the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaTodah (Menachot 77a) and the end of [the chapter entitled] HaSefinah (Bava Batra 90a). And this is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] Beit Kor (Bava Batra 104a, and there, s.v. "Pachot"), we learned in a Mishnah: "[If one says:] 'I am selling you a beit kor of land, measured with a rope' — if it was less by any amount, he deducts [from the price]; if it was more by any amount, he returns [the excess]," and Rashbam explained there that that which Rava said, that [the transaction] is reversed, his statement was not [said] regarding land — and this poses a difficulty to his explanation from here! And one can answer: that there [in Bava Batra], the seller does not say, "I measured that there is a beit kor in it," for then [the transaction] would certainly be reversed in accordance with Rava; rather, he says so in general terms, and the seller thought that there was that amount, and therefore the sale stands. And if you ask: let [the Gemara] say [in Rava's dilemma] that he knew that he sowed six [kav] and is selling it for more than its value, and since he sowed them, perhaps [the wheat] is nullified as subordinate to the land? And one can answer: in such a case, it is obvious that there is exploitation, for the sale is not dependent on the land, but rather on [the price of] wheat in the market.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:11:1.hebrew: אלא דאמר שדאי בה כדבעי לה - וא"ת: היינו מקח טעות, דבעי ליה ו' והוא לא שדא אלא ה'? וי"ל: דהמוכר מודה דלא שדא אלא ה', ואמר דלא בעי אלא ה', וקרקע זו אם זרעה כדבעי לה שוה אותם דמים — ואגלאי מילתא דבעי שיתא. וא"ת: למה לא תחשב זו אונאת קרקע, כיון שלא טעה לא במדת מנין החטין ולא בשומא, לא טעה אלא במה שלא הושבח הקרקע כדבעי לה? וי"ל: כיון דאי הוה שדא בה כדבעי לה כמו שאמר היו שוה אותם דמים, נמצא שהאונאה מן החטין ולא מן הקרקע:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:11:1.english: Rather, where he said, "I cast in it as required" - And if you say: This is a mistaken transaction, since it required six [measures] and he only cast five? And one can say: The seller admits that he only cast five, and he said that it only requires five, and [that] this land, if he sowed it as required, is worth that money — and it was discovered that it requires six. And if you say: Why should this not be considered exploitation of land, since he erred neither in the measure of the count of the wheat nor in the appraisal — he only erred in that the land was not improved as required? And one can say: Since if he had cast in it as required, as he said, it would have been worth that money, it turns out that the exploitation is from the wheat and not from the land.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:2:1.hebrew: יצאו שטרות - מדממעט להו מאונאה, משמע דחל המכר מדאוריית' בשטרות. וא"ת: פרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמז:) אמרינן מתנת שכיב מרע מדרבנן, ופריך: והאמר רב נחמן המוכר שטר חוב לחברו וחזר ומחלו מחול, ואפי' יורש מוחל, ומודה רב נחמן שאם נתנו במתנת שכיב מרע שאינו יכול למחול; אי אמרת בשלמא מתנת שכיב מרע דאורייתא, משום הכי אינו יכול למחול כו'. והשתא: והלא מכר שטר חוב דאורייתא, ואפי' הכי יכול למחול! ומפרש ר"י דה"פ: אי אמרת בשלמא דאורייתא, היינו מוהעברתם; א"כ עשאו הכתוב יורש, וא"כ אמאי יורש מוחל, מאי אולמיה דהאי יורש מהאי? אי נמי: אפי' הוי מכר שטר חוב דרבנן, משכחת ביה אונאה מדאורייתא, כגון שהלוהו על פה ונתן לו יותר מדאי כדי לעשות שטר שיעבוד, או הלוהו בשטר ונתן לו הלוה יותר מדאי שיחזיר לו השטר ויהיה מלוה על פה. ולרבינו חיים נראה דקנה מן התורה אם יש ללוה קרקעות, שמוכר לו שיעבוד שיש לו בקרקעות. ובמרובה (ב"ק דף סב:) כתבתי באריכות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:2:1.english: "Documents are excluded" - Since [the Gemara] excludes them from [the prohibition of] ona'ah (price fraud), this implies that a sale is biblically valid for documents. And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 147b), we say that a deathbed gift is rabbinic, and [the Gemara] raises a difficulty: Did not Rav Nachman say that one who sells a promissory note to his fellow and then waives it, it is waived, and even an heir can waive it; yet Rav Nachman concedes that if he gave it as a deathbed gift, he cannot waive it? Now, it is well if you say that a deathbed gift is biblical — because of this he cannot waive it, etc. And now, is not the sale of a promissory note biblical, and even so he can waive it? And Ri explains that this is what [the Gemara] means: It is well if you say it is biblical, that is from [the verse] "and you shall cause to pass" [Numbers 27:8]; if so, Scripture made him an heir, and if so, why can an heir waive it — what is the greater strength of this heir over that [one]? Alternatively, even if the sale of a promissory note is rabbinic, you can find biblical ona'ah with it, such as where he lent him orally and gave him too much [money] in order to make a lien document, or he lent him with a document and the borrower gave him too much [money] so that he would return the document to him and it would become an oral loan. And to Rabbeinu Chaim, it appears that he acquires [it] by Torah law if the borrower has land, because he is selling him the lien that he has on the land. And in [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 62b) I wrote at length.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:8:1.hebrew: והאי ביומיה מכירה הוא - תימה, דבפ' קמא דע"ז (דף טו. ושם ד"ה והשתא) מוכח דשכירות לא קני, מ"ישראל ששכר פרה מכהן" ומ"לא לבית דירה אמרו". וי"ל דהכא גבי אונאה כתיב "ממכר" מיותר, לרבות שכירות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 56b:8:1.english: And this [rental] for its day is a sale - This is puzzling, for in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (15a, and there s.v. Vehashta) it is proven that rental does not effect acquisition, from [the case of] "an Israelite who rented a cow from a priest" and from [the Mishnah stating] "they did not say [that one may rent it] for a dwelling house." And one can answer that here, with regard to exploitation (ona'ah), "a sale" (mimkar) is written superfluously, to include rental:
